The '''2026 Hartlepool Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day, to elect 12 of 36 members of [[Hartlepool Borough Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=teessidetoday |date=2026-01-25 |title=Is Your Hartlepool Councillor up for Election in May: Local Elections 2026 To Set the Stage for a Pivotal Political Contest |url=https://www.teesdurhampost.co.uk/post/is-your-hartlepool-councillor-up-for-election-in-may-local-elections-2026-to-set-the-stage-for-a-pi |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=The Teesside |language=en}}</ref>

Changes 2024–2026:
*August 2024: [[Jonathan Brash]] (Labour) resigns – by-election held September 2024<ref>{{cite news |title=Hartlepool MP steps down as councillor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgxn510261o |access-date=27 January 2026 |work=BBC News |date=11 August 2024}}</ref>
*September 2024: Owen Riddle (Labour) wins by-election<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Burn Valley Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/21262/#2024-09-19 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>
*March 2025: Cameron Sharp (Labour) resigns – by-election held May 2025<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marko |first1=Nic |title='It has been an absolute honour' Hartlepool's youngest ever Labour councillor stands down on obtaining new job |url=https://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/news/politics/hartlepool-borough-councils-youngest-ever-labour-councillor-stands-down-after-obtaining-new-job-5045690 |access-date=27 January 2026 |work=Hartlepool Mail |date=21 March 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
*May 2025: 
**Amanda Napper (Reform) gains by-election from Labour<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Throston Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/21272/#2025-05-01 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>
**Rob Darby (Conservative) joins Reform<ref>{{cite news |last1=Payne |first1=Mark |title=Why one Hartlepool councillor has decided to defect from Conservatives to Reform UK |url=https://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/news/politics/hartlepool-councillor-rob-darby-defects-from-conservatives-to-reform-uk-5121137 |access-date=27 January 2026 |work=Hartlepool Mail |date=9 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
**Tom Feeney (Labour) leaves party to sit as an independent<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boothroyd |first1=David |title=Halifax banks on Reform |url=https://www.localcouncils.co.uk/2025/05/halifax-banks-on-reform/ |website=LocalCouncils.co.uk |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>
*June 2025: Steve Wallace (Independent, elected as Labour) resigns – by-election held July 2025<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marko |first1=Nic |title=Voters face second by-election in months as Hartlepool councillor resigns |url=https://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/news/politics/voters-face-second-by-election-in-months-as-steve-wallace-resigns-from-hartlepool-borough-council-5163812 |access-date=27 January 2026 |work=Hartlepool Mail |date=5 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
*July 2025: Ed Doyle (Reform) nominally gains by-election from Labour<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Throston Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/21272/#2025-07-10 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>
*August 2025: Mike Young (Conservative) joins Reform<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marko |first1=Nic |title=Hartlepool's former Conservative leader Mike Young joins Reform UK |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cn854v2qdyjo |access-date=27 January 2026 |work=BBC News |date=7 August 2025}}</ref>
*Andrew Martin-Wells (Conservative) and Scott Reeve (Conservative) leave party to sit as independents

==Summary==

===Background===
In [[2024 Hartlepool Borough Council election|2024]], Labour gained the council from [[no overall control]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hartlepool result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E06000001 |access-date=2026-01-27 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> They held the council previously until 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-03 |title=Win for Labour in Hartlepool as they lead council for first time since 2019 |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/24296248.labour-win-hartlepool-borough-council-take-majority/ |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=The Northern Echo |language=en}}</ref>
